title: Modules Practice Exam
description: Test imports, virtual environments, pip, and running modules as scripts.

questions.prompt: What does import math do?
options: Loads the math module so you can use math.sqrt, etc.
Runs math as a script only
Copies every name into the current namespace without a prefix
questions.explanation: import math brings in the module; access members as math.name.

questions.prompt: How do you import only sqrt from math?
questions.explanation: from module import name brings sqrt into the current namespace.

questions.prompt: What is a Python module?
options: A .py file (or package) whose code can be imported
questions.explanation: Any .py file you import acts as a module; packages are folders with __init__.py.

questions.prompt: A virtual environment isolates project dependencies from the system Python.
questions.explanation: venv gives each project its own site-packages and interpreter context.

questions.prompt: Which command commonly creates a venv named .venv?
questions.explanation: python -m venv .venv creates a virtual environment in the .venv directory.

questions.prompt: What does pip install requests do?
options: Downloads and installs the requests package into the active environment
Runs all tests in your project
questions.explanation: pip installs third-party packages from PyPI (or another index).

questions.prompt: What does if __name__ == "__main__": guard?
options: Code that runs only when the file is executed directly
Code that runs only when imported
questions.explanation: __name__ is "__main__" when you run python file.py, not when importing.

questions.prompt: Where are third-party packages usually listed for reproducible installs?
questions.explanation: requirements.txt (or pyproject.toml) documents dependencies for pip install -r.

questions.prompt: When you import a module, Python may execute top-level code in that file once.
questions.explanation: Import runs the module body the first time; results are cached in sys.modules.

questions.prompt: What does import random as r allow?
questions.explanation: as assigns a local alias for the imported module.

questions.prompt: On macOS/Linux, how do you activate a venv in .venv?
questions.explanation: source .venv/bin/activate adjusts PATH to use the venv's python and pip.

questions.prompt: What is the standard library?
options: Modules shipped with Python (e.g. os, json) without pip install
questions.explanation: The standard library comes with Python; pip adds external packages.

questions.prompt: Why use pip install -r requirements.txt?
options: Install all listed packages at once for the project
questions.explanation: -r installs every requirement line from the file into the active environment.

questions.prompt: from module import * is generally discouraged in production code.
questions.explanation: Star imports pollute the namespace and make names harder to trace.

questions.prompt: If utils.py is in the same folder as main.py, how can main import utils?
options: import utils (when both are on the module search path)
utils must be a pip package only
questions.explanation: Same-directory modules are importable when the directory is on sys.path.

questions.prompt: What does python -m pip install --upgrade pip do?
options: Runs pip as a module to upgrade pip itself
questions.explanation: python -m pip invokes pip with the current interpreter, often safer than a bare pip command.

questions.prompt: Which helps avoid installing packages into the wrong Python?
options: Activate the project's venv before pip install
questions.explanation: Activating the venv ensures pip targets that environment's site-packages.

questions.prompt: What is __name__ when another file does import myapp?
questions.explanation: When imported, __name__ is the module's name, not "__main__".

questions.prompt: You can run a package module with python -m package.module.
questions.explanation: -m runs a module as a script using the proper package context.

questions.prompt: What is a common reason to split code into multiple modules?
options: Organize related code and reuse it across files
questions.explanation: Modules keep projects maintainable and let you import shared logic.
